## The continuous experiment

You will build one reusable CIFAR-10 training system, then change its hypothesis while keeping the experimental protocol visible.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[CIFAR-10] --> B[Transforms]
    B --> C[DataLoaders]
    C --> D[MLP]
    C --> E[CNN]
    D --> F[Shared train/validate API]
    E --> F
    F --> G[Scheduler + checkpoint]
    G --> H[Fair comparison]
```

The first session practices the PyTorch machinery from Chapter 6. The second session begins after convolution is taught and focuses on declaring and inspecting a CNN. Dataset, optimizer, scheduler, metric, and checkpoint interfaces remain stable.

## Session 1 · PyTorch system with an MLP

1. Inspect CIFAR-10 and define training/evaluation transforms.
2. Visualize repeated stochastic augmentations of one image.
3. Build reproducible train, validation, and test loaders.
4. Define an MLP and verify every tensor shape.
5. Compute its parameter count analytically and programmatically.
6. Configure cross-entropy, optimizers, and a learning-rate scheduler.
7. Train the same initialized model on CPU and GPU and compare measured time.
8. Save a resumable checkpoint.

## Session 2 · Replace the hypothesis with a CNN

The CNN section is explicitly reserved until convolution has been introduced. Students then:

1. declare convolutional blocks and trace spatial shapes;
2. compute the CNN parameter count;
3. train directly on GPU when available;
4. use the fixed AdamW optimizer and cosine scheduler;
5. compare the MLP and CNN under the same data split and metrics;
6. reload a checkpoint and continue training without resetting optimizer or scheduler state.

:::{.callout-important}
## Fair comparison contract

MLP and CNN runs must use the same split, class mapping, validation metric, epoch accounting, and augmentation policy. Session 2 changes the model family—not every experimental decision at once.
:::

## Assessment boundaries

At the end of Session 1, students are assessed on tensors, transforms, loaders, modules, parameter counting, loss/optimizer configuration, devices, schedulers, and checkpoints.

The CNN implementation is not a Session 1 requirement. Its scaffold is labeled as locked infrastructure until the convolution lecture. After that lecture, declaring the CNN and explaining its shape changes become assessed work.

## Submission standard

Restart the kernel and run the notebook from top to bottom for the completed session. Submit:

- passing checks for all unlocked TODOs;
- an augmentation gallery;
- MLP and CNN parameter counts with a written calculation;
- a CPU/GPU timing table with the hardware named;
- training/validation curves and learning-rate history;
- a checkpoint-resume demonstration; and
- a conclusion that separates speed, optimization, and generalization claims.
